findings.definition: Angulation is an opening divergence between the path of price bars and the path of the Alligator mouth; price must move at a steeper angle away from the Alligator.
findings.rule_1: Begin at the point where price bars cross or pass through the Alligator mouth (jaw, teeth and lips).
findings.rule_2: Trace or imagine the Alligator-mouth path; the source gives more attention to jaw and teeth than to lips.
findings.rule_3: Trace the outer edges of price bars: lower edges for an up move and upper edges for a down move.
findings.rule_4: Angulation exists only when the two paths clearly move away from each other; the angle must be increasing.
findings.negative_example: The UOPX example shows a divergent-bar shape that is invalid when prices move at a similar/parallel angle instead of angling away; the source also identifies penetration into the Alligator as invalid.
findings.consequence: A bullish or bearish divergent-bar signal is not taken without increasing angulation.

source_recheck.implementation_boundary: Do not reduce angulation to current price-to-Jaw distance, a fixed angle threshold or an invented lookback. Any future operational measurement must preserve the source's crossing-origin, path-edge, Alligator-mouth and increasing-divergence conditions, be causal on closed bars, and remain separately validated. This source review does not authorize bot or decoder changes.

cases.independent_review_question: third consecutive AO direction change and stop trigger beyond candle extreme

findings.setup_context: WM2 is the momentum-follow-through/add-on signal after an initial WM1 reversal-bar entry; the book explicitly describes it as increasing an existing position, not opening an unrelated standalone position.
findings.histogram_color: The histogram is green when the current AO bar is higher than the preceding AO bar and red when it is lower. The color describes bar-to-bar momentum change, not whether AO is above or below zero.
findings.long_sequence: For the bullish WM1 setup, AO is expected to be red initially. When momentum turns and AO bars turn green, the book says this commonly occurs within 2–4 bars after entry and that the position is usually increased after three consecutive green AO bars.
findings.long_price_trigger: Place a buy stop one tick above the high of the price bar corresponding to the third consecutive green AO bar.
findings.short_sequence: For the bearish WM1 setup, the Canadian-dollar example shows AO continuing to rise for two bars after the reversal bar; the sell signal is the third declining/red AO bar and may occur six bars after the WM1 reversal bar. The source warns not to expect it immediately.
findings.short_price_trigger: Figure 10.5 shows the add-on sell order one tick below the price bar corresponding to the third declining/red AO bar.
findings.visual_examples: Figure 10.3 illustrates three green AO bars as the add-on signal; Figure 10.4 shows the bullish example; Figure 10.5 shows the bearish example.

source_recheck.implementation_boundary: Keep WM2 as a campaign add-on candidate linked to a prior qualified WM1 position. The third consecutive rising/falling AO histogram bar identifies the corresponding price bar; the price stop trigger still has to be crossed before the add-on is considered triggered. Do not mark an order filled from the AO signal alone. This source recheck does not approve executable bot logic.

cases.independent_review_question: fractal formation vs price trigger with teeth filter AT activation

findings.formation_vs_activation: Fractal formation creates a pending candidate; completion of the pattern alone does not mean its breakout trigger has fired.
findings.buy_stop: Place the buy stop one tick above the high of the upward fractal.
findings.sell_stop: Place the sell stop one tick below the low of the downward fractal.
findings.teeth_filter_at_activation: A buy signal is used only if price is above the red balance line (Alligator Teeth) when it fires; a sell signal is used only if price is below the red line when it fires.
findings.formation_location_not_decisive: The source distinguishes where the fractal signal forms from where it fires; activation location relative to the red line determines validity.
findings.pending_lifetime: A formed fractal signal remains pending until it fires or a new fractal signal forms.
findings.valid_invalid_examples: Figures 11.5 and 11.6 contrast a valid breakout and fractals whose activation occurs on the wrong side of the Alligator Teeth.

source_does_not_establish.tie_breaking_for_multiple_overlapping_pe: Only the stated lifetime rule is explicit; a complete software selection policy is not specified.

source_recheck.engineering_implication: If closed H1 OHLC alone cannot establish whether the trigger occurred above/below the moving Teeth line at the activation instant, preserve UNRESOLVED/ABSTAIN; do not substitute candle close or the Teeth value at fractal formation. This is an engineering limitation inferred from the source timing requirement, not a Williams numeric rule.

source_recheck.page_131_finding: TC2 describes protecting an established long entry and a stop-and-reverse strategy if the qualified Fractal sell signal is hit; the cited example reverses after a bearish divergent bar.
source_recheck.pages_149_151_finding: TC2's short-side sequence specifies the bearish divergent-bar setup, protective stop, and a conditional buy-Fractal reversal; the example describes reversing to the long side after a bullish divergent bar.
source_recheck.excluded_page_164: Page 164 concerns the creative-process/morning-pages discussion, not an opposite-signal or position-management rule; it is not evidence for this review target.
source_recheck.implementation_boundary: A qualified opposite signal may establish a stop/reverse trigger; it is not an instruction to close immediately on signal appearance. Reversal depends on the specified price trigger and position sizing. This source check is not executable bot approval.
